evidence: Current sources read/edited and cached Java class bytes inspected as data. No compilation, tests, syntax checks, Java class loading, game execution, process inspection, GPU commands or exports.

reference.batching: FeatureSubmits.add obtains batchKey, uses an unbatched ArrayList when null, otherwise HashMap.computeIfAbsent(key, ArrayList) and appends the submission. The currently supported model/custom submissions use their RenderType reference as batchKey.
reference.traversal: sortFeatureInto emits unbatched then each HashMap.values batch, with strictlyOrdered=false. The dispatcher coalesces adjacent equal feature/strictness outputs within a phase. Debug maybeShuffle is a distinct optional path.
reference.clear: FeatureSubmits.clear clears unbatched and removes already-empty batch lists while clearing/retaining nonempty lists. SimpleFeatureRenderPhase.clear drops an empty feature slot or clears a nonempty one.
reference.phaseLifetime: SubmitNodeStorage drains numeric orders in ascending AVL-map order. It skips empty phases and removes an entire order only when all its phases were empty at the start of that drain. An empty simple phase's retained keys therefore survive while a different phase keeps the order alive.
reference.routing: Regular cape/wing models use solid phase 0 in order 0. Skin models use translucent-model phase 7. Base cosmetics and bent skin use custom phase 8 in order 0. Fabric CosmeticsLayer.Canvas.glow explicitly uses order(1), custom phase 8.
reference.emptyCape: Cached CapeLayer.submit checks invisibility/showCape/texture/equipment but still calls submitModel when inherited cape BODY visibility is false. ModelPart.render returns before emitting vertices; the model submission remains.

port.producer: JavaSimplePhases is retained by BedrockPlatform and used by WorldFrame.geometry after shared avatar staging. The shared Submit adapter now also serves a separate software collector in WorldFrame.render (software-simple-phase-source.json), without sharing drain history. It models only the supported source renderer's avatar scope, with debug shuffle disabled and no foreign/unbatched features.
port.keys: Real owned JavaRenderType objects with reference equality/hashCode are HashMap keys. Numeric wire IDs, pixels, texture names and insertion-order maps do not substitute for HashMap bucket traversal. These are the port renderer's hashes/history, not captured Java game objects or hashes.
port.modelAtomicity: All part batches of one model are appended as one submission; empty batches participate. An expressive emote hiding the cape model BODY now retains an empty cape submit instead of removing the phase/consolidation boundary.
port.lifetime: Each successful collection is a source collector drain, not an observed game render phase. Nonempty simple phases clear/retain used bucket lists and remove previously empty lists. Empty phases preserve retained keys while another supported phase keeps their order alive. A fully empty order is discarded.
port.epoch: Session/dimension changes and resets start a new positive monotonic epoch. Unsupported/general/anonymous inputs return unknown metadata and invalidate the history. Known world gaps and geometry parsing/staging/encoding failures reset it. The next valid collection starts a new epoch. This is not a native lease or cross-process identity.
port.wire: ARCGEO09 retains v8 batches and appends metadata after all textures: collector epoch u64 (1..i64::MAX), phase count u8 (0..3), then for each nonempty phase order u8, stage u8, count u32, count batch indices u32. ARCGEO10 uses the same records after a strict trailer-presence byte, allowing unknown simple phases independently of known model glint inputs (native-packet-glint-source.json). Valid ascending keys are (0,0),(0,8),(1,8). Phase byte budget is 9 plus 6 per phase plus 4 per simple-phase batch, within the existing 96 MiB cap. Earlier packets have unknown metadata. The Java result retains its exact WorldFrame and NativeAvatarGeometry references; the encoder rejects a result from different staging input.
port.decode: Reject invalid epoch/count/key order, unknown render references/general roles, missing solid model boundaries, oversize/truncated/index-invalid metadata, wrong phase roles, duplicates/omissions, restarted render buckets and nonascending original submit order inside a bucket. Metadata covers every supported simple-phase batch once and excludes translucent skin model batches.
port.assembly: Phase.owned_avatars requires matching epoch, distinct owning model/custom feature references, one explicit preparation per batch in storage order, and actual Java-equivalent view poses for every skin model. It inserts the existing unstable model sorter between solid and custom phases, then emits glow in order 1. All simple outputs use strictly_ordered=false; model distance outputs use true. Existing dispatcher/group/material preflight follows.
port.entry: Geometry.from_owned_avatar_inputs joins this exact Uploaded frame, source phase metadata and owning preparation/view-pose inputs before the existing no-command material/pipeline preflight. It retains ordered phase-to-group membership for record_phase rather than flattening current phase locations away. Source code remains unscheduled by the live renderer (native-avatar-phase-recording-source.json).

limitations: This is the owned source renderer's supported avatar collector. It does not reproduce an independently running Java game's identity hashes, foreign feature/cache history, optional debug shuffle, outline/crumbling/ghost variants or engine-wide phase ownership.

The producer runs on serialized explicit geometry collections, not every native/Java game frame. Its epoch/history describes those collection drains only; no equal live render frequency or timing is claimed.

Java-equivalent submitted view poses, prepared GPU equality, native material/light/target inputs, actual native world insertion and resource/fence lifetime ownership remain separate unfinished inputs.
The native owner must join this collector with other participating world submissions in their actual phases, including joint translucent ordering, before it can claim complete world ordering.
No runtime, cross-language output or visual equivalence was checked; full rendering/replay/export parity remains unverified and incomplete.
